professions.name: Advocate and solicitor

body.name: Legal Profession Qualifying Board (entry qualifications) and the Malaysian Bar (Bar Council)

route: Become a 'qualified person': an exempting law degree or English Bar call, or an LPQB-recognised law degree plus the CLP.
Pass, or be exempted from, the Bahasa Malaysia Qualifying Examination.
File a petition for admission and serve nine months of pupillage under a master.
Be admitted by the High Court as an advocate and solicitor.
Hold a valid practising certificate before practising.

sources.supports: s.3 definition of 'qualified person' (named LLB degrees, barrister-at-law of England, or other qualifications the Board declares by Gazette); s.11 admission requirements (age 18, good character, citizen or permanent resident, pupillage, Bahasa Malaysia Qualifying Examination); s.12(2) nine-month pupillage; s.36 no practice without being on the Roll and holding a practising certificate; s.37 offences for unauthorised persons.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 166, Legal Profession Act 1976 (AGC online updated text, as at 1 November 2012)

sources.supports: The LPQB sets mandatory entry requirements for West Malaysia: recognised law degrees, the UK Bar Practice Course, the CLP and the CLP exam. The Act applies to West Malaysia; Sabah and Sarawak use their own Advocates Ordinances but accept the CLP as one pathway.
sources.title: Note on the Misconceptions Surrounding the Inclusion of Sabah and Sarawak in the Legal Profession Qualifying Board (Malaysian Bar)

sources.supports: Only graduates with law degrees recognised by the LPQB can enter the legal profession; some local law degrees are not recognised.
sources.title: Admission - The Malaysian Bar

sources.supports: Example of LPQB recognition: a recognised overseas LLB makes graduates eligible to register for the CLP examination.
sources.title: Durham's LLB recognised in Malaysia (Durham University, 12 January 2026)

sources.supports: The New Bar Course will replace the CLP and is expected in 2028, or 2029 at the latest (written parliamentary reply, October 2026); the LPQB set up a task force on 27 April.
sources.title: New Bar course to replace CLP only in 2028 or 2029, Dewan Rakyat told (The Star, 5 October 2026)

sources.supports: The New Bar Course would be a three-month online Conversion Course followed by a six-month Legal Practice Postgraduate Certificate, for people who are not qualified persons.
sources.title: Govt moves to replace CLP with practice-based New Bar Course (New Straits Times, 22 June 2026)

professions.notes: Covers Peninsular Malaysia (the Malaysian Bar's 12 state bars). Sabah and Sarawak admit advocates under their own Advocates Ordinances, which currently accept the CLP. Admission also needs age 18+, good character, and Malaysian citizenship or permanent residence (s.11). Being called to the English Bar is another way to become a qualified person (s.3). Recent change: the CLP is to be replaced by the New Bar Course (three-month online Conversion Course, then a six-month Legal Practice Postgraduate Certificate); the Law Minister told Parliament in October 2026 it should start in 2028, or 2029 at the latest. Until then the CLP route stands. Which degrees are exempting or CLP-eligible changes over time; the LPQB's own website could not be opened from our network, so check its current list. The AGC text used is as at 1 November 2012; later amendments (including a 2025 bill on the Board's make-up) were not checked.

professions.name: Judge or magistrate (Sessions Court Judge, First Class Magistrate, superior court judge)

body.name: Judiciary of Malaysia (Office of the Chief Registrar, Federal Court) and the Judicial and Legal Service

route: Qualify as a lawyer: legal officers in the Judicial and Legal Service are 'qualified persons' under the Legal Profession Act 1976.
Join the Judicial and Legal Service; Sessions Court Judges and First Class Magistrates must be members.
For High Court and higher courts: ten years as an advocate or in the judicial and legal service.
Be appointed to the bench; judicial office is by appointment, not by licence.

sources.supports: s.60 (Sessions Court Judges) and s.78A (First Class Magistrates) must be members of the Judicial and Legal Service, except temporary appointments; s.59(3) Sessions Court Judges appointed by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on the Chief Judge's recommendation; s.79 Second Class Magistrates can be any fit and proper person.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 92, Subordinate Courts Act 1948 (AGC online updated text, as at 1 January 2023)

sources.supports: Quotes Article 123: judges of the Federal Court, Court of Appeal and High Courts must be citizens with ten years as an advocate or in the judicial and legal service.
sources.title: Badan Peguam Malaysia v Kerajaan Malaysia (Federal Court, 2007), judgment text on the Malaysian Bar website

sources.supports: s.3 defines 'legal officer' as a qualified person in the judicial and legal service.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 166, Legal Profession Act 1976 (AGC online updated text, as at 1 November 2012)

professions.notes: Not every magistrate needs a law qualification: Second Class Magistrates can be any fit and proper person appointed by the State Authority (s.79), and temporary acting appointments are allowed. The Federal Constitution text was read via a Federal Court judgment that quotes Article 123, because the AGC's Federal Constitution PDF returned a server error. The Judicial and Legal Service's own entry scheme was not researched. 23-1021.00 (administrative law judges, adjudicators) was left out because no Malaysian source tying it to this route was found.

professions.name: Registered medical practitioner (doctor), including specialists
route: A basic medical degree recognised by the MMC (Second Schedule), or another medical degree plus the prescribed examination.
Provisional registration with the MMC after an offer of housemanship.
Housemanship in an approved hospital: at least one year by law; the MMC programme runs two years.
Full registration with the MMC once housemanship is certified.
An annual practising certificate, with professional indemnity cover, before practising.
Specialists: recognised specialist training and qualification, then entry in the Specialist Register.

sources.supports: s.12 provisional registration (recognised qualification or other degree plus exam; citizen, spouse of citizen or permanent resident); s.13(2) at least one year of resident service (four months each in surgery, medicine, and obstetrics and gynaecology); s.14 full registration; s.14A-14C Specialist Register; s.20 annual practising certificate with indemnity cover; s.33 offences for unregistered practice and titles such as physician, surgeon, general practitioner; s.41 compulsory public service.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 50, Medical Act 1971 (AGC online updated text, as at 23 August 2022)

sources.supports: Eligibility for provisional registration (recognised Second Schedule qualification or another qualification plus the prescribed examination; offer of housemanship); certificate valid three years; endorsed 17 June 2025.
sources.title: MMC Guideline for Provisional Registration

sources.supports: Describes the two-year internship (housemanship) with four-month postings; total internship must not exceed six years.
sources.title: A Guidebook for House Officers (Malaysian Medical Council)

sources.supports: Provisional registration lets new graduates train under supervision; full registration lets a doctor practise without supervision.
sources.title: Registrations - Malaysian Medical Council

professions.notes: The Act makes it an offence for unregistered people to practise medicine or surgery, or to use titles such as physician, surgeon, doctor of medicine or general practitioner (s.33). Housemanship: the Act sets a minimum of one year, but the MMC's guidebook describes a two-year programme in practice. After full registration, doctors can be required to serve in the public service: the current Act text (s.41) says a continuous total of not less than two years, while the MMC guidebook still says three years; the Minister can reduce, exempt or postpone. Check before quoting a number. Specialist O*NET codes (cardiologists, surgeons, psychiatrists, etc.) need the extra Specialist Register step (s.14A-14C).

professions.name: Dental surgeon (dentist), including dental specialists
route: A dental qualification: an accredited local degree, or overseas training meeting the Council's standard.
Pass the Professional Qualifying Examination (some older qualifications are exempt until 31 December 2026).
Register with the Malaysian Dental Council as a dental surgeon.
Hold a valid practising certificate (CPD points and indemnity cover needed) before practising.
Specialists: an MDC-approved postgraduate qualification, then registration as a dental specialist.

sources.supports: s.29 qualifications for registration as a dental surgeon (Professional Qualifying Examination via the Dental Qualifying Committee); s.37 anyone who practises dentistry needs a valid practising certificate (CPD and indemnity cover); s.62 an unregistered person shall not practise dentistry.
sources.title: Dental Act 2018 (Act 804), LawPlayer legal database

sources.supports: Dental Act 2018 in force from 1 January 2022, replacing the Dental Act 1971; graduates must pass the Professional Qualifying Examination, except Second Schedule (1971 Act) qualification holders from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2026.
sources.title: New Dental Act effective from January (Free Malaysia Today, 10 December 2021)

sources.supports: Dentists with an MDC-approved postgraduate qualification can register as specialists in 12 fields from February 2022; the PQE exemption window is five years.
sources.title: MOH Announces New Dental Regulations Effective From 2022 (CodeBlue, 10 December 2021)

professions.notes: Section 62 makes unregistered practice of dentistry an offence (fine up to RM300,000, prison up to six years, or both). The official AGC PDF of the Dental Act 2018 returned a server error and the MDC website could not be opened from our network, so section details come from the LawPlayer database and news reports (body URL left null). Time-sensitive: the window for older Second Schedule qualifications to register without the PQE closes on 31 December 2026. The same Act registers dental therapists through the Malaysian Dental Therapists Board; no O*NET code was mapped to them.

professions.name: Registered pharmacist
route: A pharmacy qualification listed in the Act's First Schedule, or one the Minister deems suitable.
Provisional registration with the Pharmacy Board.
At least one year working as a provisionally registered pharmacist in approved premises (extendable by up to a year).
Full registration, then an annual certificate each year to stay on the register.

sources.supports: s.6 provisional registration (First Schedule qualifications, mostly Bachelor of Pharmacy degrees); s.6A(2) at least one year of employment as a pharmacist in Second Schedule premises, extendable by up to one year; s.6B full registration; s.7 restricted titles; s.11C-11D public service notice (not more than three years); s.16 annual certificate.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 371, Registration of Pharmacists Act 1951 (AGC online updated text, as at 15 April 2025)

professions.notes: The Act restricts the titles pharmacist, pharmaceutical chemist, chemist and druggist, and druggist, and the use of 'pharmacy' or 'dispensary' for retail businesses, to registered persons (s.7). Fully registered pharmacists can be required to serve in the public service (s.11C-11D). The Act applies to Peninsular Malaysia and, by extension orders noted in the Act, to Labuan and Sarawak; Sabah was not covered by that note. The Pharmacy Board's website could not be opened from our network (body URL left null), so any Board qualifying examination for some graduates was not verified.

professions.name: Registered nurse
route: Complete the prescribed nurse training at an institution approved by the Nursing Board.
Pass the Nursing Board's final examination for registration.
Register with the Nursing Board in the relevant part of the Register.

sources.supports: s.4 Register with general and supplementary parts (assistant nurses, mental health, public health, community and rural nurses); s.5(2) registration requires prescribed training in a Board-approved institution; s.10 offence to use the title 'registered nurse' or imply registration when not registered. Applies throughout Malaysia.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 14, Nurses Act 1950 (reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 January 2006)

sources.supports: Bachelor of Nursing graduates sit the Malaysia Nursing Board licensure examination; the Board sets the syllabus, runs the final examination for registration and issues registration certificates.
sources.title: Nursing graduates to registered nurses (Universiti Tunku Abdul Rahman, November 2023)

professions.notes: The Act protects the title 'registered nurse' and the Register's titles, uniforms and badges (s.10), rather than setting out a scope of practice. 29-2061.00 (licensed practical nurses) is a loose match to the Register's supplementary parts such as assistant and community nurses. Advanced US roles (nurse anaesthetists, nurse practitioners) have no separate statutory title in the Act, but they still start from nurse registration. The AGC text is the 2006 reprint; later amendments and regulations were not checked. The Nursing Board's website (Ministry of Health) could not be opened from our network, so the minimum qualification level was not confirmed (left null).

professions.name: Registered midwife
route: Pass the Midwives Board's qualifying examination, or hold a midwifery qualification the Board accepts.
Register with the Midwives Board before practising midwifery.

sources.supports: s.2 definition of midwife (care of normal childbearing women and newborns for reward; students under supervision excluded); s.3 Midwives Board; s.11 qualifications for registration (Board examination or acceptable qualifications); s.14(1) practising midwifery without registration is an offence. Applies throughout Malaysia.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 436, Midwives Act 1966 (AGC online updated text, as at 15 October 2024)

professions.notes: Unlike the Nurses Act, this Act restricts the practice itself: anyone who is not a registered midwife and practises midwifery commits an offence (s.14). Nurse midwives (29-1161.00) also need Nursing Board registration. The Act refers to an annual practising certificate (s.13D) but the details were not checked. The Midwives Board's website was not found or opened.

professions.name: Graduate Engineer / Professional Engineer (Ir.)
route: An engineering degree recognised by BEM (for example EAC-accredited or Washington Accord).
Register with BEM as a Graduate Engineer before taking a job that performs professional engineering services.
Gain practical experience; BEM asks for three years as a registered Graduate Engineer.
Pass BEM's Professional Assessment Examination, or become a Corporate Member of IEM.
Register as a Professional Engineer (Ir.); pass the Professional Competency Examination for a Practising Certificate.

sources.supports: s.2 'professional engineering services'; s.7(1) only a Professional Engineer may take up employment requiring professional engineering services or use 'Professional Engineer', 'Ir.', 'P.Eng.'; s.7(1A) Practising Certificate needed to practise or do business for designated engineering works and recover fees; s.7(1B) 'Grad.Eng.' and 'Eng.Tech.' titles; s.7(2) registered Graduate Engineers and Engineering Technologists may take such employment; s.10 qualifications; s.10D Practising Certificate; s.24A employers may only engage PEPCs or engineering consultancy practices for professional engineering services.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 138, Registration of Engineers Act 1967 (AGC online updated text, as at 1 November 2015)

sources.supports: Recognised qualifications (EAC-accredited, Washington Accord); Professional Engineer applicants need three years' registration as a Graduate Engineer and one of three routes: Professional Assessment Examination, overseas PE plus Code of Conduct Assessment, or IEM Corporate Membership.
sources.title: Registration & Renewal - BEM | Board of Engineers Malaysia

professions.notes: What the law restricts: (1) taking up employment that requires 'professional engineering services' (services and advice on feasibility, planning, survey, design, construction, commissioning, operation, maintenance and management of engineering works or projects) unless registered, so working engineers need at least Graduate Engineer registration; (2) the titles 'Professional Engineer', 'Ir.', 'P.Eng.', 'Grad.Eng.' and 'Eng.Tech.'; (3) practising or running a business providing such services for designated engineering works, submitting plans, and recovering fees, which needs a Professional Engineer with Practising Certificate. Software engineers (15-xxxx) are NOT covered by this rule: the Act protects the titles listed above, not the word 'engineer' on its own, and Kotak should not map software, data or IT 'engineer' roles here. Engineering technologists (17-3xxx) may need BEM registration as Engineering Technologists if their job performs professional engineering services (s.7(2)(aa)); they were not mapped. AGC text as at 1 November 2015.

professions.name: Architect (Ar.)

body.name: Board of Architects Malaysia (Lembaga Arkitek Malaysia, LAM)

route: LAM-recognised architecture qualifications at Part I and Part II, or pass LAM's Part I and II examinations.
Register with LAM as a Graduate Architect.
At least two years (104 weeks) of practical experience after registering.
Pass the LAM Part III Professional Examination.
Register as an Architect (Ar.); you must have lived in Malaysia for six months before applying.

sources.supports: s.7 only an Architect may use the title 'Architect' or 'Ar.', set up an architectural consultancy practice, or recover fees; s.10(1) Graduate Architect registration and the practical experience and examinations the Board sets; s.10(2) registration as Architect (or PAM Corporate Member); s.10(3) six months' residence in Malaysia.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 117, Architects Act 1967 (AGC online updated text, as at 1 March 2016)

sources.supports: Architect registration requires being a registered Graduate Architect, the prescribed practical experience, and passing the Part III Professional Examination.
sources.title: Requirements for Registration as an Architect | Lembaga Arkitek Malaysia

sources.supports: Graduate Architect registration needs a LAM-recognised qualification; others must pass the LAM Part I and II Examination (twinning and franchise programmes are not recognised).
sources.title: Requirements for Registration as Graduate Architects | Lembaga Arkitek Malaysia

sources.supports: Minimum practical experience before Part III is two years (104 weeks), completed by 1 March of the exam year.
sources.title: Part III Professional Examination Practical Experience Log Book (LAM)

sources.supports: Example of a LAM Part II programme: a two-year Master of Architecture recognised as equivalent to LAM Part II, entered after LAM Part I recognition.
sources.title: Master of Architecture (Taylor's University)

professions.notes: The Act restricts the title 'Architect'/'Ar.', setting up an architectural consultancy practice, and recovering fees for architectural consultancy services (s.7). minimum_level is 'master' because LAM Part II is normally a master's-level programme (example: Taylor's Master of Architecture); LAM's own pages do not state the award level. The Part III log book uses wording from before the 2015 amendment ('registered Architect' then 'Professional Architect'); under the current Act the steps are Graduate Architect then Architect. Landscape architects (17-1012.00) were not mapped: no Malaysian statute regulating them was found in this research.

professions.name: Interior Designer (registered with LAM)

body.name: Board of Architects Malaysia (Lembaga Arkitek Malaysia, LAM)

route: A LAM-accredited interior design degree (or LAM Part I or II architecture), or pass LAM's Qualifying Assessment.
Register with LAM as a Graduate Interior Designer.
Gain the practical experience and pass the examinations LAM sets.
Register as an Interior Designer; Corporate Members of MIID can register directly.

sources.supports: s.27A only an Interior Designer may use the title 'Interior Designer', set up an interior design consultancy practice, or recover fees as an Interior Designer; s.27D Graduate Interior Designer, practical experience and examinations, then Interior Designer (or MIID Corporate Member).
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 117, Architects Act 1967 (AGC online updated text, as at 1 March 2016)

sources.supports: Graduate Interior Designer needs a LAM-accredited interior design bachelor's (or LAM Part I plus one year's interior design work, or LAM Part II); others take the Qualifying Assessment, open only to Diploma in Interior Design holders who graduated before 2017.
sources.title: Requirements for Registration as Graduate Interior Designers | Lembaga Arkitek Malaysia

sources.supports: MIID Corporate Members or equivalent can register as Interior Designers; registered Architects can practise as Interior Designers.
sources.title: Requirements for Registration as Interior Designer | Lembaga Arkitek Malaysia

professions.notes: The Act restricts the title 'Interior Designer', setting up an interior design consultancy practice, and recovering fees for interior design advice or services (s.27A). It does not clearly stop an employee from doing design work under another job title, so Kotak's warning should focus on the title and on running an interior design practice. Registered Architects may also practise as Interior Designers.

professions.name: Professional Quantity Surveyor (PQS)
route: A quantity surveying degree accredited by BQSM.
Register as a Provisional Quantity Surveyor and join the Royal Institution of Surveyors Malaysia (RISM).
Two years' supervised experience under a PQS or CQS (three years with an external supervisor).
Pass BQSM's Assessment of Professional Competence: log book, critical analysis report and interview.
Register as a Professional Quantity Surveyor.

sources.supports: s.7(1) only a Consultant or Professional Quantity Surveyor may practise, carry on business or take up employment as a QS under titles such as 'Quantity Surveyors', 'Building Economist' or 'Project Cost Consultant'; s.7(3) consulting practice needs a Board permit; s.10 Provisional QS, practical experience, test of professional competence, then PQS or CQS.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 487, Quantity Surveyors Act 1967 (AGC online updated text, as at 1 May 2016)

sources.supports: Tier 1 PQS eligibility (valid PVQS, Malaysian address, 183 days' presence in Malaysia in the prior 12 months, supervised experience, APC pass); Graduate Route: two years' supervised training (three with an external supervisor), then critical analysis report and interview; Experience Route needs five years.
sources.title: BQSM Guideline to Two-Tier Registration, Tier 1 - Professional Quantity Surveyors (Revision 2.5, effective 29 November 2024)

professions.notes: Loose O*NET match: 13-1051.00 Cost Estimators includes estimators outside construction (for example manufacturing) whom the Act does not cover. Warn only for construction cost or quantity surveying roles. The Act restricts practising or being employed as a QS under the protected titles, and consulting practice without a Board permit (s.7). No CIP 2020 code covers quantity surveying (closest are 52.2001 Construction Management and 15.1001 Construction Engineering Technology), so qualifying_fields is empty; the qualifying degree is a BQSM-accredited QS degree.

professions.name: Licensed land surveyor (LSr)

body.name: Land Surveyors Board (Lembaga Jurukur Tanah Malaysia)

route: A degree in land surveying or geomatics recognised by the Land Surveyors Board.
Two years' articled training with a licensed land surveyor who has been registered at least five years.
Pass the Board's Part I Cadastral Practice exam, practical tasks, an oral and practical exam, and a viva voce.
Get on the Register, then hold an annual licence to practise.

sources.supports: s.9 registration (age 21, good character, Board certificate of competency after its examinations); s.10 annual licence to practise (non-citizens need the Minister's approval).
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 458, Licensed Land Surveyors Act 1958 (AGC online updated text, as at 1 March 2014)

sources.supports: Amendment Act 2024: applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; adds geomatics surveys; 'LSr' title; new s.19 offence for non-licensed people undertaking or certifying title or geomatics surveys, signing survey plans, or using the title.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act A1730, Licensed Land Surveyors (Amendment) Act 2024

sources.supports: How to become licensed: a university degree in geomatics or surveying (or Board-approved equivalent), practical training under a licensed land surveyor, and the Board's surveying examination.
sources.title: Lembaga Jurukur Tanah Malaysia

sources.supports: Detailed route: recognised land surveying degree, two years' articleship with a licensed surveyor of at least five years' standing, Part I Cadastral Practice, practical tasks, oral and practical exam, viva voce; Sabah and Sarawak have separate boards.
sources.title: Malaysia: Investment in the Services Sector, Booklet 14 Surveying Consultancy Services (MIDA, 2021)

professions.notes: Covers Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan; Sabah (Surveyors Ordinance 1960) and Sarawak (Land Surveyors Ordinance 2001) have their own boards. The law restricts title and geomatics surveys, certifying them, signing survey plans and using the title; others may do survey work only under a licensed land surveyor's immediate direction or supervision. The commencement date of the 2024 amendment (Act A1730) was not confirmed. General survey technicians (17-3031.00) were not mapped.

professions.name: Chartered Accountant, C.A.(M), and approved company auditor
route: A recognised accounting qualification (First Schedule Part I), the MIA Qualifying Examination, or membership of a recognised body (Part II).
At least three years' relevant work experience (MIA's CARE programme for the Part I and QE routes).
Register with MIA as a Chartered Accountant, C.A.(M).
To audit companies: an MIA practising certificate and approval as a company auditor by the Minister of Finance.

sources.supports: s.15 chartered accountant admission (First Schedule Part I exam plus three years' experience, Part II recognised body, or MIA Qualifying Examination plus three years); s.22 only registered chartered accountants may hold out as chartered accountant, auditor, tax consultant or tax adviser, or use 'accountant' to imply it; s.23 licensed accountants; First Schedule lists Part I programmes and Part II bodies.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 94, Accountants Act 1967 (AGC online updated text, as at 21 June 2024)

sources.supports: s.263 company auditors approved by the Minister of Finance (approval valid two years; applicants must be chartered accountants under the Accountants Act); s.264 only approved company auditors may act as company auditors.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 777, Companies Act 2016 (AGC online updated text, as at 31 January 2025)

sources.supports: Entry routes to C.A.(M): Part I qualification or MIA QE plus three years' experience (through the CARE programme), or Part II body membership.
sources.title: Entry routes - Malaysian Institute of Accountants

sources.supports: Approved company auditor criteria from 1 April 2023: C.A.(M), valid practising certificate, Public Practice Programme, six years' experience including five years' audit, 7,500 audit hours and 40 engagements, 1,800 supervisory hours, interview; applications via BLESS to the Accountant General's Department.
sources.title: Applying for Audit Licence - Malaysian Institute of Accountants

professions.notes: Be precise: the Accountants Act protects titles and public practice, not accounting work in general. Only registered chartered accountants resident in Malaysia may practise or hold out as 'chartered accountant', 'auditor', 'tax consultant' or 'tax adviser', or use 'accountant' in a way implying they are one (s.22). Bookkeeping or in-house accounting jobs do not need MIA membership. Auditing companies under the Companies Act 2016 needs approval as a company auditor by the Minister of Finance (s.263-264), valid for two years. minimum_level is null because the Part II professional-body route (ACCA, CIMA, ICAEW, CPA Australia and others) does not need a degree, and Part I also lists some diplomas.

professions.name: Approved tax agent
route: Be a professional accountant, or a person the Minister of Finance is prepared to approve.
Apply to the Minister for approval as a tax agent; approval lasts at least 24 months and must be renewed.

sources.supports: s.153(1) no one holding out as a tax agent, tax consultant or tax adviser may act for another person under the Act unless they are a tax agent; s.153(3) a tax agent is a professional accountant or person approved by the Minister; s.153(6) approval valid at least 24 months; advocates excepted.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 53, Income Tax Act 1967 (AGC online updated text, as at 1 January 2026)

sources.supports: s.22 also reserves the 'tax consultant' and 'tax adviser' titles for chartered accountants, except advocates and people authorised under another law.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 94, Accountants Act 1967 (AGC online updated text, as at 21 June 2024)

professions.notes: The restriction bites when someone holds themselves out as a tax agent, consultant or adviser and acts for clients under the Income Tax Act. Preparing returns as staff of an approved tax agent's firm, without holding out, may not be caught, so phrase the warning as 'to act for clients as a tax agent'. The Minister's approval criteria for people who are not professional accountants were not checked.

professions.name: Registered veterinary surgeon
route: A veterinary degree listed in the Act's Second Schedule.
Register with the Malaysian Veterinary Council.
Hold an annual practising certificate for approved premises before practising.

sources.supports: s.12 registration with Second Schedule qualifications (DVM and BVSc degrees, including UPM and UMK); s.17 annual practising certificate tied to suitable premises; s.23 only registered vets with a certificate can recover fees; s.33 offences for unregistered practice and titles such as veterinarian, veterinary surgeon, doctor of veterinary medicine.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 147, Veterinary Surgeons Act 1974 (AGC online updated text, as at 1 April 2018)

sources.supports: The Department of Veterinary Services is considering an examination for Malaysians with overseas veterinary degrees before they can get an APC; not finalised.
sources.title: Aspiring vets face stricter qualification requirements (The Star, 23 July 2026)

professions.notes: Unregistered practice of veterinary medicine and use of titles such as veterinarian or veterinary surgeon are offences (s.33). Possible change: as of July 2026 the Department of Veterinary Services was considering an exam for overseas-trained Malaysians before they can get an annual practising certificate; nothing finalised. The Council's website could not be opened from our network (body URL left null).

professions.name: Registered optometrist
route: An optometry qualification listed in the Act's Second Schedule (bachelor's or doctor of optometry degrees).
Register with the Malaysian Optical Council as an optometrist.
Hold an annual practising certificate before practising.

sources.supports: s.19 optometrist registration with Second Schedule qualifications; s.29 only registered persons (and medical practitioners) may practise optometry, and only optometrists may prescribe and dispense contact lenses unless the Council permits; s.32 annual practising certificate; s.35 offences for unregistered use of 'optician' or 'optometrist'.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 469, Optical Act 1991 (AGC online updated text, as at 31 March 2026)

professions.notes: 'Optometry' means measuring the powers of vision or adapting lenses or prisms to aid vision (s.2). The Council's website could not be opened from our network (body URL left null).

professions.name: Registered optician
route: An opticianry or optometry qualification listed in the Act's First Schedule (mostly diplomas).
Register with the Malaysian Optical Council as an optician.
Hold an annual practising certificate before practising.

sources.supports: s.18 optician registration with First Schedule qualifications (diplomas in optometry or opticianry and dispensing optician fellowships); s.29 only registered persons may practise optometry; s.30 opticians may prescribe and dispense contact lenses only with Council permission; s.32 annual practising certificate; s.35 offences; s.36 optical appliances sold only by or under a medical practitioner or registered person.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 469, Optical Act 1991 (AGC online updated text, as at 31 March 2026)

professions.notes: Students on a First Schedule course can be provisionally registered for their practical training (s.18(3)). Contact lens work needs Council permission for opticians (s.30). The Council's website could not be opened from our network (body URL left null).

professions.name: Physiotherapist
route: Earn a qualification recognised by the Malaysian Allied Health Professions Council.
Register with the Council (applicants must be Malaysian citizens).
Hold a practising certificate, valid for two years, before practising.

sources.supports: Section 16 (registration needs a Council-recognised qualification and Malaysian citizenship), s.17(1) (no one may practise an allied health profession unless registered), s.22 (practising certificate valid two years), s.33 (offences for unregistered practice and titles), Second Schedule (list of 16 professions). In force 1 July 2020.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 774, Allied Health Professions Act 2016 (AGC online updated text, as at 15 July 2022)

professions.name: Registered teacher (schools and kindergartens)

body.name: Registrar General of Educational Institutions and Teachers (Ministry of Education)

route: Hold teaching qualifications the Registrar General considers adequate.
Register as a teacher with the Registrar General, or hold a permit to teach while an application is pending.
Government school teachers instead join the Education Service, which is exempt from registration.

sources.supports: s.103 no one may teach in an educational institution unless registered as a teacher (exemptions: Education Service members in government and government-aided institutions, permit holders, trainees in ministry training institutions); s.106 Registrar General may refuse registration if qualifications are inadequate; s.109 registration; s.114 permits to teach; s.2 'educational institution' includes kindergartens and any place where persons are habitually taught, but not religion-only teaching.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 550, Education Act 1996 (AGC online updated text, as at 1 July 2020)

professions.notes: The Act requires registration but does not fix a degree; the Registrar General judges whether qualifications are adequate, so qualifying_fields and minimum_level are left empty. The scheme for appointing government teachers to the Education Service (usually via a teaching degree) was not researched. Postsecondary teachers were not mapped: Part VII of the Act excludes private higher educational institutions, and Part IX's application to universities was not checked.

professions.name: Registered valuer

body.name: Board of Valuers, Appraisers, Estate Agents and Property Managers (LPEPH)

professions.law: Valuers, Appraisers, Estate Agents and Property Managers Act 1981
route: A valuation degree recognised by the Board (or pass the Board's examinations).
Register as a Probationary Valuer and for the Test of Professional Competence.
Two years' practical training in Malaysia under a registered valuer.
Pass the oral Test of Professional Competence, register as a valuer and get an authority to practise.

sources.supports: s.18 probationary valuer, practical experience and Test of Professional Competence; s.19 valuation work (land, buildings, plant, machinery and other effects); s.21 only registered valuers or appraisers with an authority to practise may use titles such as 'Valuer', 'Appraiser', 'Property Consultant', or undertake valuation work for a fee.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 242, Valuers, Appraisers, Estate Agents and Property Managers Act 1981 (AGC online updated text, as at 1 August 2018)

sources.supports: Valuer route: Malaysian citizen or permanent resident, Board-recognised degree, probationary valuer, two years' supervised training in Malaysia, oral Test of Professional Competence.
sources.title: FAQs - Board of Valuers, Appraisers, Estate Agents and Property Managers (LPEPH)

sources.supports: Probationary Valuer registration needs at least a degree.
sources.title: Registration - Board of Valuers, Appraisers, Estate Agents and Property Managers (LPEPH)

professions.notes: Must be a Malaysian citizen or permanent resident (LPEPH FAQ). 13-2022.00 (personal and business property appraisers) is included because s.19 covers plant, machinery, equipment and other effects; valuing shares or businesses may fall outside. The Board's old site (lppeh.gov.my) said in October 2026 that it is moving to lpeph.gov.my. CIP 52.1501 (Real Estate) is the nearest match to Malaysian estate management or valuation degrees.

body.name: Board of Valuers, Appraisers, Estate Agents and Property Managers (LPEPH)

sources.supports: Estate agent route: exam entry needs SPM with five passes (three credits) or higher; property degree holders are partly exempt; probationary estate agent; two years' supervised training; oral TPC; Malaysian citizen or permanent resident.

sources.supports: Probationary Estate Agent registration needs at least a diploma.

body.name: Board of Valuers, Appraisers, Estate Agents and Property Managers (LPEPH)

professions.law: Valuers, Appraisers, Estate Agents and Property Managers Act 1981
route: A Board-recognised degree, or pass the Board's Professional Qualifying Examination for Property Managers.
Register as a Probationary Property Manager and keep a log book for at least two years.
Submit the log book and practical task, then pass the Test of Professional Competence interview.
Register as a property manager and get an authority to practise.

sources.supports: s.22I property management practice (leases, budgets, building and facilities management, advice); s.22J only registered property managers with an authority to practise may use 'Property Manager' or 'Managing Agent', act as a property manager, or do that work for a fee; owners managing their own property are excepted.

sources.supports: Property manager steps: recognised qualification or Professional Qualifying Examination, Probationary Property Manager, log book of at least two years plus practical task, TPC interview, then Registered Property Manager.

sources.supports: Probationary Property Manager registration needs at least a degree.
sources.title: Registration - Board of Valuers, Appraisers, Estate Agents and Property Managers (LPEPH)

professions.notes: O*NET 11-9141.00 also covers community association managers and leasing managers; any role that manages other people's property for a fee falls under s.22J. Candidates with over ten years in a Board-registered firm may be considered for exemption from the log book (LPEPH FAQ).

professions.name: Certified wireman (competent person, Energy Commission)
route: Complete Form Five and two years' wiring experience with a registered electrical contractor or private wiring unit.
Pass the Energy Commission's wireman competency examination (SKM Level 2 holders can be exempted for PW1).
Receive a Certificate of Competency (grades PW1 to PW4) from the Energy Commission.

sources.supports: s.2 'competent person' means a holder of a certificate of competency issued by the Commission; s.23 installations must be worked or operated by, or under the control of, people holding prescribed qualifications and certificates; s.33C electrical work is carried out by, or under the control of, a competent person.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 447, Electricity Supply Act 1990 (AGC online updated text, as at 1 November 2023)

sources.supports: Wireman eligibility (Malaysian citizen, 18+, completed Form Five, two years' wiring experience with a registered contractor or private wiring unit, Bahasa Malaysia); SKM Level 2 exemption for PW1; grades PW1 to PW4.
sources.title: Wireman | Suruhanjaya Tenaga

professions.notes: The detailed duty to use certified competent persons for wiring is in the Electricity Regulations 1994, which were not opened; the Act's s.23 and s.33C and the 'competent person' definition were. Only Malaysian citizens can sit the wireman examination. Higher competencies (chargeman, electrical supervisor, competent electrical engineer) have separate certificates. Not degree-based.

professions.name: Licensed pilot (commercial or airline transport pilot licence)
professions.law: Civil Aviation Act 1969; Civil Aviation Regulations 2016
route: Be at least 18, with working English, SPM credits in five subjects (or an MQA-recognised degree) and a Class 1 medical.
Train at a CAAM-approved flight training organisation.
Pass the theoretical knowledge examinations and skill test.
Receive a Commercial Pilot Licence from CAAM; airline captains later need an Airline Transport Pilot Licence (age 21+).

sources.supports: reg. 53 a person may act as flight crew of a Malaysian aircraft only with an appropriate licence; reg. 59 licence classes the Director General grants (commercial, multi-crew, airline transport pilot, flight engineer); reg. 60 medical certificate requirement; reg. 61 examinations and tests.
sources.title: P.U. (A) 97/2016, Civil Aviation Regulations 2016 (in operation 15 April 2016)

sources.supports: CPL eligibility: age 18, working English, Class 1 medical, SPM credits in five subjects (or MQA-recognised degree with CGPA 3.0 and SPM credits), CAAM-approved FTO training, theory exams and skill test.
sources.title: Commercial Pilot Licence - CAAM

sources.supports: ATPL: age 21, working English, Class 1 medical, practical experience, theory exams and a skill test at an Approved Training Organisation.
sources.title: Airline Transport Pilot License - CAAM

professions.notes: Flight engineers (part of 53-2011.00) need a flight engineer licence under the same regulation. Flight hour minimums are in CAAM's CAGM 1001, which was not opened. The AGC lists the 2016 Regulations under the Civil Aviation Act 1969 (Act 3); the licensing requirement cited is in the Regulations.

professions.name: Licensed air traffic controller
route: Complete a course of training approved by CAAM's Director General.
Pass the examinations and tests the Director General specifies.
Hold an air traffic controller licence with the right rating; trainees work only under direct supervision.

sources.supports: reg. 149 no one may act or hold out as an air traffic controller, or supervise or train one, without a licence and appropriate rating (trainees under direct supervision excepted); reg. 151 validity; reg. 152 approved training and examinations.
sources.title: P.U. (A) 97/2016, Civil Aviation Regulations 2016 (in operation 15 April 2016)

professions.notes: Entry and medical requirements for air traffic controllers were not checked on the CAAM website.

professions.name: Licensed financial planner (Capital Markets Services Representative's Licence)
route: A degree or professional qualification recognised by the Malaysian government, or five years' relevant experience.
An SC-accepted planning qualification: CFP or IFP (FPAM), RFP or Shariah RFP (MFPC), or ChFC (MFPAA), with membership.
Be engaged as a representative of a firm licensed for financial planning.
Hold a Capital Markets Services Representative's Licence for financial planning from the SC.

sources.supports: s.58 no one may carry on a business in a regulated activity without a Capital Markets Services Licence; s.59 no one may act as a representative for a regulated activity without a representative's licence; Schedule 2 lists financial planning as a regulated activity and defines it as analysing someone's finances and providing a plan, fee or not.
sources.title: Laws of Malaysia Act 671, Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 (AGC online updated text, as at 5 February 2024)

sources.supports: CMSRL minimum qualifications for financial planning: degree or professional qualification (or five years' experience), and CFP/IFP with FPAM, RFP/Shariah RFP with MFPC (or three set modules with associate status), or ChFC with MFPAA.
sources.title: Licensing Handbook SC-GL/LH-2007 (R18-2024), Securities Commission Malaysia (revised 1 October 2024)

professions.notes: The licence is needed whether or not a fee is charged. Advice on insurance products may separately need Bank Negara Malaysia approval under the Financial Services Act 2013 (not checked). Insurance agents (41-3021.00) were not added: the Financial Services Act 2013 text does not itself set an agent licence, and the industry-association registration rules were not confirmed from a primary source.

professions.name: Registered T&CM practitioner (chiropractic)
route: A Bachelor Degree in Chiropractic, or equivalent, recognised by the T&CM Council.
Provisional registration with the Traditional and Complementary Medicine Council (unless exempted).
Register as a practitioner in the recognised practice area.
Hold a valid practising certificate before practising.

sources.supports: s.21 practice only in recognised practice areas; s.22 provisional registration; s.23 registration; s.25 non-registered persons may not practise (offence); s.26 practising certificate.

professions.name: Registered T&CM practitioner (traditional Chinese medicine, including acupuncture)
route: A Bachelor Degree in traditional Chinese medicine, or in acupuncture, moxibustion and tuina, recognised by the Council.
Provisional registration with the Traditional and Complementary Medicine Council (unless exempted).
Register as a practitioner in the recognised practice area.
Hold a valid practising certificate before practising.
